scope: The six previously unresolved publications in the retained sixty. Replaces their earlier working classifications for the combined cohort; historical reports remain dated snapshots.
method: Assistant manual review of fifteen purposively selected saved public posts after local keyword/title retrieval across all saved public texts for these six. Fourteen full saved texts and one opening/selected-passage reading. This is not an exhaustive reading of the six archives, an independently validated coding, or a time-varying ideology estimate.
classification_rule: Use own explicit ideological self-description or affirmative, repeated policy/editorial positions. Separate outlet role, party coalition, quoted speakers and guest authors from broad ideology. Nonpartisan reporting is not automatically centrist.

rows.coalition: Democratic-friendly electoral framing; nonpartisan accuracy claim retained
rows.organization: Multi-author electoral news, data and commentary service
rows.rationale: The outlet’s own May 2024 podcast introduction calls efforts to thwart abortion rights a cynical ploy and describes the rights at stake as cherished civil rights. Its March introduction favors greater representation of progressive mothers, while the August election digest uses favorable reproductive-rights and redistricting-reform framing. Together these support a provisional liberal editorial tendency. This goes beyond predicting Democratic gains, fundraising arrangements or Daily Kos origins. Nonpartisan reporting claims are preserved as the outlet’s stated professional role; no complete economic platform or shared ideology of every byline is inferred.

rows.coalition: Opposes politicized DOJ and transactional pardons; party identity not established
rows.organization: Individual-led legal analysis and rule-of-law advocacy
rows.rationale: Oyer’s welcome essay defines a focused legal mission. Her lecture explicitly advocates equality, public defense and redemption; her pardon analysis praises relief from excessive drug sentences while defending victim restitution, accountability and principled review. These establish a civil-liberties and clemency-reform orientation, with some liberal-compatible positions, but not a sufficiently broad or distinctive left/right/centrist platform. Former career government service and anti-Trump advocacy do not decide that label.
